what.text: This page follows refugees from the Central African Republic in all host countries combined.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 674222 Central African refugees, and Cameroon hosts the largest share, 41.2%.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo and Chad are the next largest hosts.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of the Central African Republic in several periods since 2001.
From 2009 to 2014 the groups fighting the government include the CPJP, Seleka and anti-Balaka; from 2017 to 2025 they include anti-Balaka, the UPC and the CPC.

when.text: The main years of displacement in the data are 2014 to 2025, after big changes between 2012 and 2014.
UNHCR's figure rose from 15000 in 1982 to a peak of 759187 in 2023.
Returns to the Central African Republic were highest in 2017 in UNHCR's returns data.

how.text: These are year-end totals of refugees; asylum seekers are counted in a separate series.
People displaced inside the country are counted separately by UNHCR and by IDMC, and their figures are never added.
The sources don't say which routes people took.
